overview: The CC Energy & Environment Committee serves as an advisory body for Medford's municipal energy programs, climate resilience policies, and environmental conservation efforts. Operating through the 2024-2025 and 2026-2027 terms, the committee monitors citywide emissions, reviews zoning changes for stormwater management, and coordinates large-scale public outreach events like the Harvest Your Energy Festival. A primary ongoing function is the oversight of the city's Climate Action and Adaptation Plan, ensuring progress on over 150 identified action points. As of late 2026, the committee's work is centered on performing a five-year review of that plan while investigating new regulatory frameworks for rodenticides, data centers, and light pollution.

threads.name: Municipal Energy and Electrification
threads.summary: The committee monitors the 'Electrify Medford' program, which provides residents with coaching for heat pump adoption and home energy improvements. On the municipal side, the body tracks energy consumption trends, noting a 19% reduction in building emissions between 2009 and 2024. Major infrastructure projects discussed include school HVAC upgrades, solar installations at the McGlynn School, and a planned municipal wind turbine repair. The committee also pursues grants for on-street electric vehicle charging sites and evaluates fleet electrification policies.

threads.name: Tree Preservation and Ordinances
threads.summary: Working alongside Trees Medford, the committee has been instrumental in drafting and revising a new public tree ordinance for the city. This initiative involved mapping landmark trees and advocating for state-level bond funding to support municipal reforestation efforts. By mid-2026, the City Council Committee of the Whole issued a favorable vote on the ordinance language. Ongoing projects include organizing Miyawaki mini-forest plantings and supporting a discounted residential tree program.

threads.name: Waste Reduction and Trash Policy
threads.summary: The committee manages various zero-waste initiatives, including a project to phase out black plastic takeout containers in local restaurants. In early 2026, the body engaged in a significant debate regarding the city's proposed transition to bi-weekly trash collection, balancing environmental goals with concerns about rodent control and service reductions. Members also coordinate reuse events like the 'free flea market' and specialty recycling collections. Recent work includes evaluating the claims of specialty waste companies and researching model ordinances for broader zero-waste outreach.

threads.name: Climate Action and Adaptation Plan Tracking
threads.summary: In late 2025, the committee established a systematic process for monitoring the implementation of the city's Climate Action Plan. Members utilize a spreadsheet to track progress across approximately 150 distinct climate action points, identifying areas where the city has met goals or requires more focus. This effort evolved into a formal five-year review process in late 2026. The committee plans to perform a gap analysis and dedicate specific meeting time to reviewing individual sections of the plan moving forward.

threads.name: Rodenticide Restrictions and Wildlife Protection
threads.summary: The committee has consistently researched the ecological impact of anticoagulant rodenticides on local wildlife. Early work focused on public health advisories and state-level legislative tracking regarding rodenticide alternatives. In 2026, the body hosted presentations from Save Arlington Wildlife to discuss municipal strategies for banning or restricting these chemicals. The committee is currently evaluating alternative pest management methods to advocate for a local ban on harmful anticoagulants.

threads.name: Harvest Your Energy Festival
threads.summary: The committee is responsible for the annual coordination of the Harvest Your Energy Festival, which serves as its primary public engagement event. This involves managing vendor logistics, coordinating electronics recycling, and organizing educational activities for residents. The festival has featured demonstrations on thin-film plastic recycling and provided a venue for publicizing heat pump coaching. Every year, the committee reviews logistics and participation data to refine the festival's focus on waste management and renewable energy.

threads.name: Zoning and Emerging Regulatory Research
threads.summary: Members frequently review and propose new zoning requirements to address climate resilience, such as a 'green score' for large developments to encourage permeable surfaces. The committee has expanded its focus to include research into 'dark skies' lighting ordinances to mitigate light pollution. Recent discussions have also addressed the environmental demands of data centers, specifically their impact on grid capacity and heat generation. The body intends to consult with city planners to develop regulatory frameworks for these emerging issues.
